questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Peru?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Peru article.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Peru?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Peru on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Peru article.

questions.proof: Peru is bordered to the north by Ecuador and Colombia, to the east by Brazil, to the south by Chile, and to the southeast by Bolivia.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Peru?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “History” part of the Peru article.

questions.proof: Spanish is still the main language of the people, although many also speak Quechua, the Inca language.

questions.prompt: What money is used in Peru?

hints.nudge: Money names often come from a country’s own words. The other three are spent in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Economy and tourism” part of the Peru article.

questions.proof: The currency of Peru is the Nuevo Sol.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “In March _____, Kuczynski resigned following political scandals and Vice President Martín Vizcarra was sworn-in as the next president.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twenty-first century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Peru article.

questions.proof: In March 2018, Kuczynski resigned following political scandals and Vice President Martín Vizcarra was sworn-in as the next president.
